answer: Your records do not show a blood clot in your lung. On 8 July 2025 you had a CT angiogram of the chest, the scan used to look for clots in the lungs (a pulmonary embolism). The report says: No pulmonary embolism. Lungs are clear. There was no fluid around the lungs or heart. It also noted mild wear-and-tear changes in the upper back bones. A D-dimer blood test that day was raised, at 0.92 mg/L FEU, where the record's reference limit is 0.49. A raised D-dimer does not prove a clot, and the scan is what settles it. A pulmonary embolism was recorded against that visit, but it was later marked as refuted, meaning it was ruled out. The chest pain you had was recorded as chest wall pain, and that was marked resolved by 22 July 2025. The records do not include the doctor's notes, so if you want to be sure what was discussed, ask your doctor.
